objective: A price written in Canadian, Australian or NZ dollars is read as a US-dollar price. server/services/cash/figures.ts ~L26 maps USD to ['$','US$'] and ~L95 builds the pattern with no boundary before a one-character symbol, so readMoneyFigures('Pays C$1,200 per job','USD') returns 120000 USD cents, 'Budget A$500 and NZ$300' returns two USD figures, and '$12 000' returns $12 — a silently truncated amount. CLAUDE.md §30: a price is read, never produced, and the failure mode is missing a figure, never inventing one. Fix: a single-character symbol must not be preceded by a letter (so C$, A$, NZ$ stop matching bare $), and a match immediately followed by a space and three digits is refused rather than returned partially.
expectedOutcome: C$/A$/NZ$ figures are no longer read as USD, and a space-grouped number is refused rather than truncated.

acceptanceConditions.statement: tests/cashFiguresCurrencyPrefix.test.ts: readMoneyFigures('C$1,200','USD') and readMoneyFigures('A$500 NZ$300','USD') return [], while readMoneyFigures('C$1,200','CAD') still returns 120000 cents.
Existing cash tests pass and the repository typechecks.

rollbackRequirement: Revert the commit; no schema or data change.
